step1_analysis.description: A dynamic latch or comparator likely used in the quantizer of the delta-sigma modulator. It features a cross-coupled PMOS pair (XM2, XM7) for regeneration, an NMOS reset/equalization switch (XM11), and a PMOS input pair (XM1, XM3, with gates merged to N7 in this extraction) driven by a programmable NMOS tail current array (XM4, XM5, XM8, XM10).

paper_reference.title: A 12-mW ADC Delta–Sigma Modulator With 80 dB of Dynamic Range Integrated in a Single-Chip Bluetooth Transceiver

dynamic_range.description: Dynamic range of the delta-sigma modulator

sky130_expected.calculation: System-level metric, depends on oversampling ratio (OSR) and noise shaping order.
sky130_expected.reasoning: Comparable performance can be achieved in 130nm with similar OSR and thermal noise (capacitor sizing) constraints.

sky130_expected.calculation: System-level metric derived from FFT of the output bitstream.
sky130_expected.reasoning: Depends heavily on op-amp linearity and switch sizing, which scale reasonably well in sky130 at 1.8V.

power_consumption.description: Total power consumption of the modulator

sky130_expected.calculation: P = VDD * I_total. For a single comparator, I ~ 100uA -> 0.18mW. Total ADC ~ 5-10mW.
sky130_expected.reasoning: Sky130 at 1.8V generally consumes less power than 0.35um at 2.7V for equivalent speeds.

sky130_expected.calculation: Determined by the external clock frequency applied to the switches and comparators.
sky130_expected.reasoning: Sky130 transistors have higher fT than 0.35um, easily supporting >32MHz sampling rates.

dc_gain.description: DC gain of the op-amp used in the integrators

sky130_expected.calculation: Gain = gm * ro. Requires cascoding or gain enhancement techniques.
sky130_expected.reasoning: Achieving 87dB in 130nm usually requires two stages or regulated cascodes due to lower intrinsic gain (ro) compared to older nodes.

regeneration_time.description: Time taken for the latch to resolve the input difference to full logic levels

sky130_expected.reasoning: With W=5u and L=0.5u, gm is moderate, yielding ~200ps regeneration time for a 0.5pF load.

step3_testbench.description: Testbench to measure DC power, AC gain (in reset state), and transient regeneration time of the dynamic latch.
step3_testbench.spice:
* Testbench for Dynamic Latch / Comparator
.lib "${SKY130_PDK}" tt

.param W_xm1=5u L_xm1=0.5u
.param W_xm2=5u L_xm2=0.5u
.param W_xm3=5u L_xm3=0.5u
.param W_xm4=5u L_xm4=0.5u
.param W_xm5=5u L_xm5=0.5u
.param W_xm6=5u L_xm6=0.5u
.param W_xm7=5u L_xm7=0.5u
.param W_xm8=5u L_xm8=0.5u
.param W_xm9=5u L_xm9=0.5u
.param W_xm10=5u L_xm10=0.5u
.param W_xm11=5u L_xm11=0.5u

XM1 N3 N7 N0 VDD sky130_fd_pr__pfet_01v8 l={L_xm1} w={W_xm1}
XM2 N0 N1 N2 VDD sky130_fd_pr__pfet_01v8 l={L_xm2} w={W_xm2}
XM3 N3 N7 N1 VDD sky130_fd_pr__pfet_01v8 l={L_xm3} w={W_xm3}
XM4 N3 LABEL_NET_0 GND GND sky130_fd_pr__nfet_01v8 l={L_xm4} w={W_xm4}
XM5 N3 LABEL_NET_2 GND GND sky130_fd_pr__nfet_01v8 l={L_xm5} w={W_xm5}
XM6 N5 N6 GND GND sky130_fd_pr__nfet_01v8 l={L_xm6} w={W_xm6}
XM7 N1 N0 N2 VDD sky130_fd_pr__pfet_01v8 l={L_xm7} w={W_xm7}
XM8 N3 LABEL_NET_3 GND GND sky130_fd_pr__nfet_01v8 l={L_xm8} w={W_xm8}
XM9 N4 N6 GND GND sky130_fd_pr__nfet_01v8 l={L_xm9} w={W_xm9}
XM10 N3 LABEL_NET_5 GND GND sky130_fd_pr__nfet_01v8 l={L_xm10} w={W_xm10}
XM11 N1 LABEL_NET_7 N0 GND sky130_fd_pr__nfet_01v8 l={L_xm11} w={W_xm11}

* Power and Bias Sources
VVDD VDD 0 1.8
VN2 N2 0 1.8
VN7 N7 0 0.9
VLABEL_NET_0 LABEL_NET_0 0 0.9
VLABEL_NET_2 LABEL_NET_2 0 0.9
VLABEL_NET_3 LABEL_NET_3 0 0.9
VLABEL_NET_5 LABEL_NET_5 0 0.9
VLABEL_NET_6 N6 0 0.9
* Reset clock: High to short outputs, Low to evaluate
VLABEL_NET_7 LABEL_NET_7 0 PULSE(1.8 0 5n 0.1n 0.1n 10n 20n)

* Input Signal (AC and DC)
VCM VCM 0 0.9
VAC_DIFF IN_DIFF 0 DC 0.1 AC 1
E1 N0_DRIVE VCM IN_DIFF 0.5
E2 N1_DRIVE VCM IN_DIFF -0.5
R1 N0_DRIVE N0 100k
R2 N1_DRIVE N1 100k

* Load Capacitors
C1 N0 0 0.5p
C2 N1 0 0.5p

* Differential Output
E_diff OUT_DIFF 0 N0 N1 1

.control
* DC Operating Point
op
let power = -i(VVDD) * 1.8
print power

* AC Analysis
ac dec 100 1 1G
let gain_db = vdb(OUT_DIFF)
meas ac dc_gain find gain_db at=10
meas ac bandwidth when gain_db=0 fall=1

* Transient Analysis
tran 0.1n 40n
meas tran v_max max v(N0)
meas tran v_min min v(N0)
* Measure regeneration time: from clock falling (evaluation starts) to output reaching 1V difference
meas tran regen_time trig v(LABEL_NET_7) val=0.9 fall=1 targ v(OUT_DIFF) val=1.0 rise=1
quit
.endc
